# go-humanize

`go-humanize` is a small Go library for formatting machine values into
human-readable English. It intentionally stays narrow: bytes, durations,
relative time, numbers, ordinals, percentages, and count phrases.

## Canonical API

- `Bytes(int64) string`: decimal byte formatting using `KB`, `MB`, `GB`,
  `TB`, `PB`, `EB`
- `BinaryBytes(int64) string`: IEC binary byte formatting using `KiB`,
  `MiB`, `GiB`, `TiB`, `PiB`, `EiB`
- `Number(int64) string`: comma-separated integer formatting
- `Percent(float64) string`: takes a fraction, so `0.333` returns `33.3%`
- `Duration(time.Duration) string`: compact duration formatting with at most
  two descending units
- `Relative(target, ref time.Time) string`: relative-time formatter
- `Ordinal(int64) string`: ordinal suffix formatting
- `Count(int64, singular, plural string) string`: count phrase with comma
  separators
- `ParseBytes(string) (int64, error)`: parses canonical `Bytes` /
  `BinaryBytes` text
- `ParseDuration(string) (time.Duration, error)`: parses canonical `Duration`
  text

## Error Contract

- Parse failures wrap `ErrInvalid`; callers should use
  `errors.Is(err, humanize.ErrInvalid)`

## Behavior

- Bytes output uses at most one decimal place
- `Bytes` is decimal because user-facing products (Finder, AWS/GCP consoles,
  consumer storage) use decimal byte units
- `BinaryBytes` is the developer/sysadmin variant (memory, block devices)
- `Percent` accepts a fraction: `Percent(0.5)` → `"50%"`, not `"0.5%"`
- `ParseBytes` requires `"<number> <unit>"` and only accepts text that
  round-trips through `Bytes` or `BinaryBytes`
- `ParseBytes` rejects leading or trailing whitespace
- Duration output uses at most two descending units
- `ParseDuration` accepts only text that round-trips through `Duration`
- `ParseDuration` rejects leading or trailing whitespace
- `Relative` cutovers: `<1s` just now, `60s` minute, `60m` hour, `24h` day,
  `7d` week, `30d` month, `345d` year
- Months are `30` days; years are `365` days
- Humanized text is for display only — never feed it back into protocols,
  schedulers, billing, or audit

## Non-goals

- Locale-aware formatting
- Custom separator APIs
- Precision knobs like `BytesN`
- Friendly calendar words like `yesterday` or `tomorrow`
- Text utilities or truncation helpers
- Builders, config structs, or formatting options
